title: Visually Grounded Reasoning across Languages and Cultures

bias_targets.methodology: Constructing a multicultural vision-and-language benchmark (MaRVL) using visual concepts and images selected by native speakers from five diverse cultures, visualizing image feature distributions (UMAP) to show out-of-distribution concepts, and measuring the performance degradation of state-of-the-art multimodal models compared to their performance on Western-centric datasets.

Evaluating zero-shot and translation-based cross-lingual transfer of vision-and-language models on image descriptions written by native speakers of Indonesian, Mandarin Chinese, Swahili, Tamil, and Turkish. The study also analyzes the depth of ImageNet concepts in WordNet to demonstrate the over-specificity and English-centric nature of existing lexical databases.
